opinions.quote: [I] built my own harness. I had trouble with both claude and codex. In particular, managing multiple tasks in a kanban, syncing between my machines, making sure work is done on the right machine

opinions.name: ChatGPT / Codex
opinions.point: poor at multi-task tracking and cross-machine syncing

opinions.name: Custom harness
opinions.point: easy to build, used constantly; highly recommends it
opinions.quote: [My own harness:] This kind of software is so easy to make nowadays… I'm using it all the time. I highly recommend doing so (building your own personal work management software in 2026).

opinions.name: Custom orchestration
opinions.point: tmux board very convenient for their workflow
opinions.quote: [I built] A little board in tmux I pull up with a key combination, some indicators of activity / needs me to take a look at it… Very convenient for me, probably useless to most!

opinions.name: Anthropic API
opinions.point: Opus plus Gemini best cost-performance combo
opinions.quote: Opus used for the final design/architecture reviews and some of the more complex RCA fixes… for my usage the best option was Opus + Gemini.

opinions.name: Google / Gemini API
opinions.point: low token usage with very good performance
opinions.quote: Gemini goes a long way with low token usage but delivers very good performance… I basically treat Gemini like a junior dev.

opinions.name: Claude Code
opinions.point: fun remote Android vibe coding from phone
opinions.quote: Claude code is running on a build machine VM. I use my phone Claude app to remotely build android apps… It's been pretty fun to vibe code android apps on the fly!

opinions.name: ChatGPT / Codex
opinions.point: Pro 100 plan is all they need
opinions.quote: [For AI subscriptions,] I'm subscribed to ChatGPT Pro 100. That's all I need.

opinions.name: Codex
opinions.point: too many dependencies and supply-chain risk
opinions.quote: My goal is to replace Codex in the long run. Way too many dependencies and supply chain attack opportunities to my taste.

opinions.name: Custom harness
opinions.point: handles plans and context resets, works until done
opinions.quote: my personal harness handles writing a plan in the FS, handing information over to next session, and resetting its context, so I get something similar to an orchestrator… it can handle many tasks without stopping until it's done.

opinions.name: OpenCode
opinions.point: tried logging into MySQL with a harvested password
opinions.quote: My OpenCode one day was like "and now I'm signing into your local mysql instance with your (plaintext) pw that I picked up last week to make some schema updates… and I was like, ok we're done here.

opinions.name: Claude Code
opinions.point: disables its own sandbox; untrustworthy implementation
opinions.quote: Claude frequently has decided to disable its own sandbox when I've had it running so I absolutely do not trust their implementation.

opinions.name: Claude Code
opinions.point: can disable its own sandbox
opinions.quote: I have also experienced this [Claude disabling its own sandbox]. Now I run Claude Code (or preferably Pi) inside a bubblewrap instance spawned and controlled by me that the agentic harness cannot disable

opinions.name: Pi
opinions.point: preferred over Claude Code
opinions.quote: Now I run Claude Code (or preferably Pi) inside a bubblewrap instance spawned and controlled by me that the agentic harness cannot disable by it's own choice.

opinions.name: ZeroStack
opinions.point: likes it, unsure its sandbox truly protects
opinions.quote: Also used by ZeroStack… which I quite like, but whether it provides 'meaningful' protection am less sure.

opinions.name: DeepSeek
opinions.point: unbeatable price, improving fast
opinions.quote: I'm using Deepseek-v4.1-flash via both a direct subscription and OpenRouter. The price is unbeatable, and the latest versions are advancing in leaps and bounds.

opinions.name: OpenCode
opinions.point: works really well; no reason to look further
opinions.quote: For coding, I'm using Opencode/Openchamber. There's probably better options around nowadays, but it's working really well for me so I haven't bothered looking further.

opinions.name: Hermes Agent
opinions.point: overnight research feels like a superpower
opinions.quote: Probably 70% of the time I'll kick off Hermes late in the day to research or build something complex overnight, then pick it up the following morning. That alone feels like a superpower

opinions.name: Muse
opinions.point: good at interactive coding sessions
opinions.quote: [I use] Muse Glimmer (because it is good at what it is optimised for: interactive coding sessions).

opinions.name: Gemma
opinions.point: really super for creative research and planning
opinions.quote: enjoying the really super Gemma 4 12B QAT when working on creative photography research or non-code planning

opinions.name: Pi
opinions.point: better at small contexts; good for learning
opinions.quote: Pi is just much better in smaller context sizes, and it is the right fit if you are keen to learn from first principles.

opinions.name: OpenCode
opinions.point: couldn't get on with it; messy source code
opinions.quote: I tried OpenCode first. I couldn't quite get on with it and what ultimately made me switch was trying to understand its terribly messy source code.

opinions.name: Osaurus
opinions.point: impressive, but wants more sandbox control
opinions.quote: I did some experiments with Osaurus (really quite impressive) and I actually think that is almost enough by itself, except that I want a little more control over the sandbox container.

opinions.name: Antigravity
opinions.point: main driver; good at search
opinions.quote: Antigravity (AGY - Google Ultra $100/month)… My main driver because it's pretty good at search compared to setting something up with DSH.

opinions.name: DeepSeek
opinions.point: very cheap, except pricier during Chinese daytime
opinions.quote: DeepSeekHarness (DSH) Desktop using:… with pay as you go DeepSeek tokens, more expensive to use during my night/Chinese daytime, otherwise very cheap

opinions.name: Goose
opinions.point: didn't work for their needs

opinions.name: OpenClaw

opinions.name: Codex

opinions.name: Antigravity

opinions.name: Custom orchestration
opinions.point: light, hackable, and works really well
opinions.quote: [My custom orchestration is] not nearly as polished as some of the software factory setups and fancy GUI orchestrators I'm seeing, but it's light, hackable, and so far the bitter lesson has kept this working really well for me

opinions.name: Muse
opinions.point: too unreliable, too many privacy concerns
opinions.quote: I have been trying out Muse for a while but it hasn't found a solid place in my life yet. Still too unreliable and too many privacy concerns to justify giving it a lot of access.

opinions.name: ChatGPT / Codex
opinions.point: best value thanks to usage resets
opinions.quote: I use other models via Open Router, but ChatGPT beats them in value (at the moment) thanks to Tibo's resets.

opinions.name: Custom orchestration
opinions.point: Claude coordinating Codex agents saves time
opinions.quote: I mostly make Claude coordinate a group of Codex agents… This saves me time because it's easier to talk to one agent than a group of agents.

opinions.name: Ctlflow
opinions.point: agent swarms surface surprising insights from data
opinions.quote: For non coding usecases, I use https://www.ctlflow.com. This lets me run dozens of agents on tasks like equity analysis. The information a swarm of agents can surface from a large data store can be quite surprising.

opinions.name: Zed
opinions.point: super fast, intuitive, open source

opinions.name: Custom assistant

opinions.name: Local model (unspecified)

opinions.name: Entrim

opinions.name: Mistral

opinions.name: Maki

opinions.name: T3 Code

opinions.name: T3 Code
opinions.point: great workflow, phenomenal remote sessions, joy to use
opinions.quote: I just recently started using T3 Code and it's strongest points are having a really good workflow… and truly phenomenal remote sessions… it has been a joy to work with.

opinions.name: T3 Code
opinions.point: better in every regard than other harnesses
opinions.quote: It's just baffling to me how it [T3 Code] is better in every regard than every other harness that I've ever tried… I can't imagine using anything else right now.

opinions.name: Pi

opinions.name: Ollama Cloud

opinions.name: Pi

opinions.name: Claude Code

opinions.name: Claude Code

opinions.name: OpenClaw
